metadata.case_name: NG LING AND OTHERS v. MAK WAI AND OTHERS

injuries.description: As a result of an accident that occurred at Tuen Mun Road at about 2 p.m. on the 4th of December 1979 Cheung Hong Hung was fatally injured
source: As a result of an accident that occurred at Tuen Mun Road at about 2 p.m. on the 4th of December 1979 Cheung Hong Hung was fatally injured and LI KIN HONG suffered injuries to his left leg and hand.
he suffered a broken left femur, and laceration of the left hand, the left thigh and the left calf.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of other parts of wrist or hand

source: he suffered a broken left femur, and laceration of the left hand, the left thigh and the left calf.
The broken thigh was treated with an intramedullary nail.

injuries.description: laceration of the left thigh and the left calf; the two lacerations on the leg required skin grafts
source: he suffered a broken left femur, and laceration of the left hand, the left thigh and the left calf.
The two lacerations on the leg required skin grafts.

injuries.description: small piece of foreign body in inner thigh (removed under local anaesthesia)
source: Later a small piece of foreign body was removed from his inner thigh under local anaesthesia.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration with foreign body of hip or thigh

manifestations.description: The extent of the deceased's injuries were such that he died shortly after the accident.
used 2 walking sticks for six weeks after discharge
The two lacerations on the leg required skin grafts.
Dr Wedderburn found a 4% impairment of the leg.
He stated if the nail is removed all symptoms will disappear and he felt a 1% permanent disability would be fair.
some foreign body discomfort (presence of the nail caused some foreign body discomfort and recommended its removal)

treatments_received: The broken thigh was treated with an intramedullary nail.
The two lacerations on the leg required skin grafts.
Transferred to Pok Oi Hospital for a further 3 weeks
Used 2 walking sticks for six weeks after discharge
A small piece of foreign body was removed from his inner thigh under local anaesthesia
treatments_future: Removal of the intramedullary nail (recommended by Dr Wedderburn)

losses.description: General damages (future loss of dependency) calculated as 2,000 x 12 x 15 = $360,000 (award for benefit of deceased's family)
Pain, suffering and loss of amenities awarded to 3rd Plaintiff for injuries to left leg and hand (award $15,600)
Temporary reduced mobility (used two walking sticks for six weeks) and 4% impairment of the leg
